content: {"id": "a38582c6-1e59-4d73-9055-7219576b11aa", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "On a RHEL 8 EC2 instance, a security update for nodejs won't install during patching. dnf says 'package nodejs-16... is filtered out by modular filtering'. The nodejs:14 module stream is enabled. How do I get the security update to apply?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
{"id": "3b113090-2034-491c-b5b5-9a7c0d67daf4", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "chat_title", "title": "RHEL 8 nodejs modular filtering blocking security update"}]}

{"id": "0d05e45e-b983-4d41-af26-834d7c6252a4", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "This is a classic RHEL 8 **modularity + AppStream** issue, not an AWS-specific problem — so let me explain what's happening and how to fix it directly.

## What's going on

RHEL 8's AppStream repo ships `nodejs` as a **module** with multiple streams (`10`, `12`, `14`, `16`, etc.). You have the `nodejs:14` stream enabled, so dnf's modular filtering **hides every package from other streams** — including the `nodejs-16` security update — even though it's a valid newer package. This is intentional module behavior, not a repo or AWS issue.

## How to fix it

You have two real options:

### Option 1 — Switch module streams (recommended if 16 is the intended target)
```bash
dnf module switch-to nodejs:16
```
This resets the stream, removes/reinstalls packages tied to the old stream, and lets the newer `nodejs-16` package install cleanly. Check compatibility with your app first — this is a stream switch, not a minor bump.

### Option 2 — Get the latest security build within your current stream (14)
If you want to **stay on nodejs:14** but still get the security fix, check whether a patched build exists *within* stream 14:
```bash
dnf module list nodejs
dnf update nodejs --allowerasing
```
If RHEL has backported the CVE fix into a `14.x` z-stream build, a normal `dnf update` within the enabled stream will pick it up without any filtering issue. If no fixed build exists in stream 14 and the fix only landed in stream 16, you must switch streams (Option 1) — there's no way to force an unrelated stream's RPM in without switching, since `--nobest` or disabling filtering (`dnf --disablerepo=*modular update nodejs`) only pulls from non-modular repos and generally won't resolve correctly for AppStream content.

### Checking which stream has the fix
```bash
dnf module info nodejs --all
```
Look at which stream version contains the CVE-fixed release before deciding.

## For patch automation (SSM Patch Manager)
If this is failing during an SSM Patch Baseline run, the same modular filtering applies — Patch Manager calls dnf under the hood and will hit the identical "filtered out by modular filtering" error. The fix still has to happen at the module level (switch stream or confirm an in-stream fix), not via patch baseline rules. Patch baselines can only approve/skip the package name — they can't bypass module filtering.
